study_identification_part.si_4_title: Detecting accelerated retinal decline in mental disorders through normative modeling

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study used optical coherence tomography (OCT) data from the UK Biobank database. Healthy controls (N=56,545) were used for normative model development, and separate patient populations with mental disorders (SZ N=171, BD N=265, MDD N=102) were compared against the normative model.

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: UK Biobank healthy controls (HC) were used to build sex- and laterality-specific GAMLSS normative models for retinal thickness metrics. Patients with schizophrenia (SZ), bipolar disorder (BD), and major depressive disorder (MDD) were then compared to the normative decline to assess disease-related deviations. The study also performed robustness checks with 80-20 cross-validation for training/testing split.

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was built using GAMLSS framework with all 56,545 healthy controls from UK Biobank. The manuscript mentions 80-20 cross-validation for robustness checks (80% training = ~45,236, 20% testing = ~11,309), but the main analysis used all HC subjects for model training. Sex- and laterality-specific models were built for each retinal metric (macular thickness, RNFL, GC-IPL).
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "To estimate normative retinal decline, we used these measurements from N = 56,545 healthy individuals from the UK Biobank who had complete OCT imaging data for all retinal metrics (54.8% female; see Table 1 for demographics)" ... "A random 80% sample of the HC population was chosen at each iteration to train the normative models for each metric"
